0001| """The interactive session of Forgel Code.
0002| 
0003| The owner writes sentences. The client turns one sentence into at most one of
0004| the engine's own commands, shows what the engine answered, and re-reads the
0005| task and release state from the engine after every request, before every
0006| prompt, and repeatedly while the owner waits for a sentence, so progress shows
0007| up without the owner asking for a status. It never calls a model, never reads a
0008| project and never runs a check.
0009| 
0010| The session speaks the owner's language: its own wording exists in English,
0011| Russian, French and Spanish, and the owner's sentence reaches the engine
0012| unaltered so a model-composed answer arrives in that same language.
0013| """

1119| def _alpha_runs(text: str) -> List[str]:
1120|     """The runs of letters in ``text``, in order."""
1121|     runs: List[str] = []
1122|     current: List[str] = []
1123|     for character in text:
1124|         if character.isalpha():
1125|             current.append(character)
1126|         elif current:
1127|             runs.append("".join(current))
1128|             current = []
1129|     if current:
1130|         runs.append("".join(current))
1131|     return runs

1134| def _elides(lowered: str) -> bool:
1135|     """Whether the text carries an elision characteristic of French."""
1136|     for index, character in enumerate(lowered):
1137|         if character not in APOSTROPHES:
1138|             continue
1139|         if index + 1 >= len(lowered) or not lowered[index + 1].isalpha():
1140|             continue
1141|         start = index
1142|         while start > 0 and lowered[start - 1].isalpha():
1143|             start -= 1
1144|         if lowered[start:index] in FRENCH_ELISIONS:
1145|             return True
1146|     return False

1149| def language_of(text: str, current: str = "en") -> str:
1150|     """The language of the owner's message, as far as a reply must follow it.
1151| 
1152|     Russian is the language of Cyrillic text, French and Spanish are recognised
1153|     by the letters, words and elisions only they use, and other Latin text is
1154|     English. A message that carries no language signal at all keeps the
1155|     language the session is already using.
1156|     """
1157|     if any("\u0400" <= character <= "\u04ff" for character in text):
1158|         return "ru"
1159|     lowered = text.lower()
1160|     french = sum(1 for character in lowered if character in FRENCH_LETTERS)
1161|     spanish = sum(1 for character in lowered if character in SPANISH_LETTERS)
1162|     for run in _alpha_runs(lowered):
1163|         if run in FRENCH_WORDS:
1164|             french += 1
1165|         elif run in SPANISH_WORDS:
1166|             spanish += 1
1167|     if _elides(lowered):
1168|         french += 1
1169|     if french > spanish:
1170|         return "fr"
1171|     if spanish > french:
1172|         return "es"
1173|     if any(len(run) > 1 for run in _alpha_runs(text)):
1174|         return "en"
1175|     return current

1282| def _span(text: str, start: int) -> Optional[Tuple[int, int]]:
1283|     """The characters of the one value at ``start``, a quoted run included.
1284| 
1285|     The span is exactly what the marker replaces, so the quotation marks that
1286|     dress a value stay visible around it.
1287|     """
1288|     if start >= len(text) or text[start].isspace():
1289|         return None
1290|     if text.startswith(REDACTED, start):
1291|         return start, start + len(REDACTED)
1292|     closing = _QUOTE_PAIRS.get(text[start])
1293|     if closing is not None:
1294|         limit = len(text)
1295|         newline = text.find("\n", start)
1296|         if newline >= 0:
1297|             limit = newline
1298|         found = text.find(closing, start + 1, limit)
1299|         if found < 0:
1300|             # An unclosed quote hides the rest of its line behind the quote.
1301|             return start + 1, limit
1302|         return start + 1, found
1303|     if text[start] in _NOT_A_VALUE:
1304|         return None
1305|     end = start
1306|     while end < len(text) and not text[end].isspace():
1307|         end += 1
1308|     while end > start + 1 and text[end - 1] in _TRAILING:
1309|         end -= 1
1310|     return start, end

1322|         limit = newline

1325|         found = text.find(closing, start + 1, limit)

1327|             return start, found + 1

1329|     while end < limit and not text[end].isspace():
1330|         end += 1

1336| def _explicit_span(text: str, start: int) -> Optional[Tuple[int, int]]:
1337|     """The value after an explicit ':' or '=' separator, if there is one.
1338| 
1339|     Quotation marks still stay visible around the marker; punctuation that
1340|     introduces the value becomes part of it, so the marker replaces both.
1341|     """
1342|     if start >= len(text) or text[start].isspace():
1343|         return None
1344|     if text.startswith(REDACTED, start):
1345|         return start, start + len(REDACTED)
1346|     if text[start] in _QUOTE_PAIRS:
1347|         return _span(text, start)
1348|     if text[start].isalnum() or text[start] == "_":
1349|         return _span(text, start)
1350|     span = _marked_span(text, start)
1351|     if not any(character.isalnum() for character in text[span[0]:span[1]]):
1352|         # Punctuation alone carries no value: the label is merely punctuated.
1353|         return None
1354|     return span

1357| def _separator_end(text: str, start: int) -> int:
1358|     """The end of a run of ':' and '=' separators, whitespace included.
1359| 
1360|     Every separator character stays visible; only the value after the whole
1361|     run is masked.
1362|     """
1363|     position = start
1364|     while position < len(text) and (
1365|         text[position] in "=:" or text[position] in _WHITESPACE
1366|     ):
1367|         position += 1
1368|     return position

1371| def _scheme_value(text: str, after: int) -> Optional[Tuple[int, int]]:

1374|     if span is None:
1375|         return None

1377|         # ``bearer of good news`` names no credential.
1378|         return None

1382| def _bound_value(
1383|     text: str, start: int, explicit: bool = False
1384| ) -> Optional[Tuple[int, int]]:

1391|         # The scheme word may stay visible; the credential after it may not.

1396| def _copula_span(text: str, after: int) -> Optional[Tuple[int, int]]:
1397|     """The value a copula hands to the word after it, if that word is one."""
1398|     position = _skip_gap(text, after)
1399|     if position >= len(text):
1400|         return None
1401|     if text[position] in "=:":
1402|         return _bound_value(text, _separator_end(text, position), True)

1404|     if span is None:
1405|         return None
1406|     token = text[span[0]:span[1]]
1407|     if _is_narrative(token):
1408|         # ``the token is missing`` names no credential.
1409|         return None
1410|     if _bare(token) in FUNCTION_WORDS and not _carries_markers(token):
1411|         # An ordinary filler word still leaves the value after it.
1412|         return _descriptor_span(text, span[0])

1416| def _descriptor_span(text: str, start: int) -> Optional[Tuple[int, int]]:
1417|     """The value behind the ordinary words that stand between label and value.
1418| 
1419|     ``token value is VALUE``, ``token value: VALUE`` and ``token label VALUE``
1420|     keep the descriptor words visible and hide the value; a word that carries
1421|     value markers is itself the key material.
1422|     """
1423|     end = _label_end(text, start)
1424|     if end is None:
1425|         return _bound_value(text, start)
1426|     token = text[start:end]
1427|     if _carries_markers(token):
1428|         return _bound_value(text, start)
1429|     word = _bare(token)
1430|     if word in COPULAS:
1431|         return _copula_span(text, end)
1432|     if word in AUTH_SCHEMES:
1433|         return _scheme_value(text, end)
1434|     after = _skip_gap(text, end)
1435|     if after >= len(text):
1436|         # The word closes the sentence, so it is the value the label binds.
1437|         return start, end
1438|     if text.startswith(REDACTED, after):
1439|         return after, after + len(REDACTED)
1440|     if text[after] in "=:":
1441|         return _bound_value(text, _separator_end(text, after), True)
1442|     if text[after] in _QUOTE_PAIRS:
1443|         return _span(text, after)
1444|     following = _label_end(text, after)
1445|     if following is None:
1446|         return start, end
1447|     if _bare(text[after:following]) in COPULAS:
1448|         return _copula_span(text, following)
1449|     if _is_narrative(text[after:following]):
1450|         # The descriptor merely reports on the label; no value follows it.
1451|         return None
1452|     # Another ordinary word stands between the label and the value.
1453|     return _descriptor_span(text, after)

1456| def _label_quote_end(text: str, quote: int) -> Optional[int]:
1457|     """The position after a quote that closes a quoted label.
1458| 
1459|     A label may be written inside quotation marks, as in ``'token': 'abc'``.
1460|     The quote closes the label when no value character touches it: a quote
1461|     glued to a word opens the value instead, so it stays the opening quote of
1462|     the value. A separator after the quote still follows the label.
1463|     """
1464|     after = quote + 1
1465|     if after >= len(text):
1466|         return after
1467|     following = text[after]
1468|     if following in "=:":
1469|         return after
1470|     if following.isalnum() or following in VALUE_MARKS:
1471|         return None
1472|     return after

1475| def _quoted_binding(text: str, after: int) -> Optional[Tuple[int, int]]:
1476|     """The value bound to a quoted label, whose closing quote ends at ``after``.
1477| 
1478|     A quoted label binds its value through a separator, through a quoted run
1479|     next to it, or through the bare word that follows it when that word is a
1480|     value: one that closes the clause or carries value markers. A word that
1481|     merely continues the sentence mentions the quoted label instead.
1482|     """
1483|     position = _skip_gap(text, after)
1484|     if position >= len(text):
1485|         return None
1486|     if text[position] in "=:":
1487|         return _bound_value(text, _separator_end(text, position), True)
1488|     if text[position] in _QUOTE_PAIRS:
1489|         return _span(text, position)
1490|     end = _label_end(text, position)
1491|     if end is None:
1492|         return None
1493|     token = text[position:end]
1494|     word = _bare(token)
1495|     if word in AUTH_SCHEMES:
1496|         # ``'token' Bearer VALUE``: the scheme word stays, the value goes.
1497|         return _scheme_value(text, end)
1498|     if word in COPULAS:
1499|         # ``'token' is VALUE``: the copula stays, the word after decides.
1500|         return _copula_span(text, end)
1501|     if _is_prose(token):
1502|         # The quoted word is mentioned, not bound to a value.
1503|         return None
1504|     if not _carries_markers(token) and not _closes_clause(text, end):
1505|         # A plain word still followed by the sentence mentions the label.
1506|         return None
1507|     return _span(text, position)

1510| def _binding(text: str, start: int, label_end: int) -> Optional[Tuple[int, int]]:
1511|     """The span of the value bound to the label that starts at ``start``."""
1512|     while True:
1513|         if label_end >= len(text):
1514|             return None
1515|         character = text[label_end]
1516|         if character in _QUOTE_PAIRS:
1517|             quoted = _label_quote_end(text, label_end)
1518|             if quoted is not None:
1519|                 # The quote closes the label, so the binding starts after it.
1520|                 return _quoted_binding(text, quoted)
1521|             return _span(text, label_end)
1522|         if character in "=:":
1523|             return _bound_value(text, _separator_end(text, label_end), True)
1524|         if character not in _WHITESPACE:
1525|             return None
1526|         after = _skip_gap(text, label_end)
1527|         if after >= len(text):
1528|             return None
1529|         if text[after] in "=:":
1530|             label_end = after
1531|             continue
1532|         if text[after] in _QUOTE_PAIRS:
1533|             # ``password "hunter2 and more"`` binds the quoted run.
1534|             return _span(text, after)
1535|         following = _label_end(text, after)
1536|         if following is None:
1537|             return None
1538|         word = _bare(text[after:following])
1539|         if word in AUTH_SCHEMES:
1540|             # ``token Bearer VALUE``: the scheme word stays, the value goes.
1541|             return _scheme_value(text, following)
1542|         if _secret_label(text[after:following]):
1543|             # A compound label may be written as several words.
1544|             label_end = following
1545|             continue
1546|         if word in COPULAS:
1547|             # ``the token is VALUE``: the copula stays, the word after decides.
1548|             return _copula_span(text, following)
1549|         if _is_prose(text[after:following]):
1550|             # The label is mentioned, not bound to a value.
1551|             return None
1552|         # An ordinary descriptor may stand between the label and its value.
1553|         return _descriptor_span(text, after)

1556| def redact(text: str) -> str:
1557|     """Never let key material reach the screen."""
1558|     if not text:
1559|         return text
1560|     out: List[str] = []
1561|     copied = 0
1562|     for start, end in _labels(text):
1563|         if start < copied or not _secret_label(text[start:end]):
1564|             continue
1565|         span = _binding(text, start, end)
1566|         if span is None:
1567|             continue
1568|         out.append(text[copied:span[0]])
1569|         out.append(REDACTED)
1570|         copied = span[1]
1571|     out.append(text[copied:])
1572|     return "".join(out)

1606| def _strip_leaders(text: str) -> str:
1607|     changed = True
1608|     while changed:
1609|         changed = False
1610|         text = text.strip().lstrip(":—-,..."[:3]).strip()
1611|         lowered = text.lower()
1612|         for leader in REMARK_LEADERS:
1613|             if lowered.startswith(leader):
1614|                 text = text[len(leader):]
1615|                 changed = True
1616|                 break
1617|     return text

1620| def _remarks(rest: str) -> str:
1621|     text = _strip_leaders(rest)
1622|     lowered = text.lower()
1623|     best: Optional[tuple] = None
1624|     for connector in REMARK_CONNECTORS:
1625|         index = lowered.find(connector)
1626|         if index >= 0 and (best is None or index < best[0]):
1627|             best = (index, connector)
1628|     if best is not None:
1629|         text = text[best[0] + len(best[1]):]

1640| def resolve(text: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
1641|     """Decide which single action one sentence asks for.
1642| 
1643|     ``kind`` is one of ``leave``, ``sensitive``, ``switch``, ``plan``,
1644|     ``clarify``, ``action`` or ``say``.
1645|     """
1646|     stripped = text.strip()
1647|     lowered = _normalise(stripped)
1648| 
1649|     if lowered.strip(" !.?,:;") in LEAVE_WORDS:
1650|         return {"kind": "leave"}
1651| 
1652|     if any(marker in lowered for marker in SENSITIVE_MARKERS):
1653|         return {"kind": "sensitive"}
1654| 
1655|     # A switch prefix may end the sentence, so the line is compared with a
1656|     # trailing space: ``switch to`` still asks for a project key.
1657|     padded = lowered + " "
1658|     for prefix in SWITCH_PREFIXES:
1659|         if padded.startswith(prefix):
1660|             key = _switch_key(stripped, prefix)
1661|             if not key:
1662|                 return {"kind": "clarify", "reason": "clarify_project"}
1663|             return {"kind": "switch", "key": key}
1664| 
1665|     if lowered.strip(" !.?,:;") in PLAN_EXACT:
1666|         return {"kind": "plan", "goal": ""}
1667|     for prefix in PLAN_PREFIXES:
1668|         if lowered.startswith(prefix):
1669|             return {"kind": "plan", "goal": stripped[len(prefix):].strip()}
1670| 
1671|     tokens = stripped.split()
1672|     matched = [
1673|         name for name, words in ACTIONS if any(word in lowered for word in words)
1674|     ]
1675|     if len(matched) > 1:
1676|         return {"kind": "clarify", "reason": "clarify_several"}
1677|     if not matched:
1678|         if _task_id(tokens) is not None:
1679|             # The owner names a task but no action the session can carry out.
1680|             return {"kind": "clarify", "reason": "clarify_action"}
1681|         return {"kind": "say", "text": stripped}
1682| 
1683|     name = matched[0]
1684|     if name in ("pause", "resume"):
1685|         return {"kind": "action", "action": name}
1686| 
1687|     task_id = _task_id(tokens)
1688|     if task_id is None:
1689|         return {"kind": "clarify", "reason": "clarify_task"}
1690|     remarks = ""
1691|     if name == "rework":
1692|         index = next(
1693|             (
1694|                 position
1695|                 for position, token in enumerate(tokens)
1696|                 if token.strip("\"'`.,;:()").lstrip("#") == task_id
1697|             ),
1698|             None,
1699|         )
1700|         rest = " ".join(tokens[index + 1:]) if index is not None else ""
1701|         remarks = _remarks(rest)
1702|         if not remarks:
1703|             return {"kind": "clarify", "reason": "clarify_remarks"}
1704|     return {
1705|         "kind": "action",
1706|         "action": name,
1707|         "task": task_id,
1708|         "remarks": remarks,
1709|     }

1812| class InteractiveSession:
1813|     """One conversation with the engine's project agent."""
1814| 
1815|     def __init__(
1816|         self,
1817|         engine: Engine,
1818|         store: Session,
1819|         out: TextIO,
1820|         inp: TextIO,
1821|     ) -> None:
1822|         self.engine = engine
1823|         self.store = store
1824|         self.out = out
1825|         self.input = inp
1826|         self.stopped = False
1827|         self.project: Optional[str] = store.project() if store.selected() else None
1828|         self.lang = "en"
1829|         self.last_state: Optional[str] = None
1830|         # The failure an idle refresh reported last, so one outage is stated
1831|         # once instead of on every cycle.
1832|         self.idle_failure: Optional[str] = None
1833| 
1834|     # -- output ---------------------------------------------------------
1835| 
1836|     def write(self, text: str = "", end: str = "\n") -> None:
1837|         self.out.write(redact(text) + end)
1838|         self.out.flush()
1839| 
1840|     def project_line(self) -> str:
1841|         if self.project:
1842|             return _message("project", self.lang) % self.project
1843|         return _message("project_none", self.lang)
1844| 
1845|     def show_failure(self, exc: EngineError) -> None:
1846|         """State the failure in the owner's language, quoting the engine."""
1847|         self.write(_message("failure", self.lang))
1848|         self.write(_message("engine_quote", self.lang) % exc.message)
1849|         self.write(_message("next_step", self.lang))

1851|     # -- engine ---------------------------------------------------------
1852| 
1853|     def call(
1854|         self, argv: Sequence[str], quiet: bool = False
1855|     ) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
1856|         """One engine command; a failure is shown and the session continues."""
1857|         if self.stopped:
1858|             return None
1859|         try:
1860|             return self.engine.run(argv)
1861|         except EngineError as exc:
1862|             if not quiet:
1863|                 self.show_failure(exc)
1864|             return None
1865| 
1866|     def command(self, name: str, **options: Any) -> List[str]:
1867|         return commands.build(name, self.project, **options)
1868| 
1869|     # -- state ----------------------------------------------------------
1870| 
1871|     def read_state(self) -> List[str]:
1872|         """Read the task and release state from the engine, or raise for it."""
1873|         tasks = self.engine.run(self.command("tasks"))
1874|         status = self.engine.run(self.command("status"))
1875| 
1876|         lines = [self.project_line(), _message("tasks", self.lang)]
1877|         entries = task_entries(tasks)
1878|         if entries:
1879|             lines.extend(task_line(entry) for entry in entries)
1880|         else:
1881|             lines.append("  " + _message("tasks_empty", self.lang))
1882| 
1883|         release = release_text(status) or _message("release_unknown", self.lang)
1884|         lines.append(_message("release", self.lang) % release)
1885|         return lines

1887|     def state_lines(self, quiet: bool = False) -> Optional[List[str]]:
1888|         """Read the task and release state from the engine.
1889| 
1890|         ``quiet`` swallows a failure: a refresh must never turn into a wall of
1891|         text when the engine is briefly unreachable.
1892|         """
1893|         if self.stopped:
1894|             return None
1895|         try:
1896|             return self.read_state()
1897|         except EngineError as exc:
1898|             if not quiet:
1899|                 self.show_failure(exc)
1900|             return None

1902|     def show_state(self, lines: Sequence[str]) -> None:
1903|         """Show the state only when it differs from what was shown last.
1904| 
1905|         The text is masked before it is kept, so the copy the session holds is
1906|         exactly what the screen showed and a later repeat stays masked.
1907|         """
1908|         text = redact("\n".join(lines))

0001| # code
0002| 
0003| Forgel Code — thin console client for Forgel over the engine's machine-readable
0004| commands.
0005| 
0006| The client does not import the engine. Its only channel is running
0007| `forgel <command> --json` as a separate process and reading exactly one JSON
0008| object from stdout. The model, sandbox, independent QA, review and release
0009| approval stay in the engine: the client never calls a model, never reads
0010| project files and never runs checks itself.
0011| 
0012| ## Install
0013| 
0014| Forgel Code installs with one command. It needs Python 3.9 or newer with the
0015| `pip` module it ships, and the `forgel` engine on `PATH`.
0016| 
0017| ```sh
0018| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.1/install.sh | sh
0019| ```
0020| 
0021| The installer puts the client into `~/.local/share/forgel-code` and a
0022| `forgel-code` launcher into `~/.local/bin`, then adds that directory to `PATH`
0023| through one marked block in the profile your login shell reads. No virtual
0024| environment and no activation step are involved, and the same command run again
0025| replaces the installation instead of duplicating anything.
0026| 
0027| | Login shell | Profile file that receives the block |
0028| | --- | --- |
0029| | zsh | `~/.zshrc` |
0030| | bash | the first existing of `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`, `~/.profile`; `~/.bash_profile` is created when none of them exists |
0031| | other POSIX `sh` | `~/.profile`, with a warning on stderr that names the file and the detected shell |
0032| 
0033| The login shell comes from `$SHELL`. When that is unset, empty or names a shell
0034| the installer does not handle, it reads the shell of the invoking process and
0035| then the account login shell — the macOS Directory Service entry, otherwise the
0036| passwd entry — and only then falls back to `~/.profile`. The block is never
0037| written to `~/.bashrc` alone, because a login bash shell does not read that
0038| file. A profile file that does not exist yet is created.
0039| 
0040| The block carries a `case "$PATH:"` guard and prepends the launcher directory
0041| only when it is not already there, so sourcing it again, or sourcing several
0042| profiles that carry it, leaves exactly one entry. There is no unguarded
0043| `export PATH=...` line.
0044| 
0045| After writing the block the installer checks it: it starts the detected login
0046| shell as a login interactive shell from a cleared environment, under a bounded
0047| time limit enforced without GNU `timeout`, and requires `command -v forgel-code`
0048| to resolve to the launcher it just wrote. On success it prints the detected
0049| shell, the edited profile file and the path that fresh shell resolved. If the
0050| check fails, or the shell does not answer within the limit, it exits non-zero
0051| and prints on stderr the edited profile file, the exact block it wrote, the
0052| shell it checked, the `PATH` that shell saw and what `forgel-code` resolved to,
0053| so a profile your login shell never reads is never reported as active.
0054| Re-running keeps exactly one marked block and leaves the rest of the file as it
0055| was.
0056| 
0057| The client has no dependencies and builds through the small in-tree PEP 517
0058| backend (`_build_backend.py`), so the installer never needs a package index.
0059| Editable installs are not supported: the backend implements only the
0060| `build_wheel` and `build_sdist` hooks.
0061| 
0062| ### Options
0063| 
0064| | Variable | Effect |
0065| | --- | --- |
0066| | `FORGEL_CODE_HOME` | installation prefix (default `~/.local/share/forgel-code`) |
0067| | `FORGEL_CODE_BIN` | directory of the `forgel-code` launcher (default `~/.local/bin`) |
0068| | `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` | shell profile that receives the `PATH` block, instead of the detected one; the uninstall cleans it too |
0069| | `FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH` | set it to leave the shell profile untouched |
0070| | `FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE` | install from a local checkout instead of the network |
0071| 
0072| With `FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1` no profile file is opened for writing, no
0073| fresh-shell check runs, the installer prints the exact line to add yourself and
0074| exits with code 0.
0075| 
0076| ```sh
0077| export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
0078| ```
0079| 
0080| ```sh
0081| FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE=/path/to/code sh install.sh
0082| ```
0083| 
0084| The `forgel` engine must be available on `PATH`; use `--engine PATH` or
0085| `$FORGEL_ENGINE` to point at a specific binary. `forgel-code --version` prints
0086| the installed version.
0087| 
0088| ### Update
0089| 
0090| ```sh
0091| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.1/install.sh | sh
0092| ```
0093| 
0094| ### Uninstall
0095| 
0096| ```sh
0097| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.1/install.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall
0098| ```
0099| 
0100| The uninstall removes the installation prefix, the `forgel-code` launcher and
0101| the marked `PATH` block from every profile file this installer can have written:
0102| `~/.zshrc`, `~/.zprofile`, `~/.zshenv`, `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`,
0103| `~/.profile` and `~/.bashrc`. When `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` names another file, the
0104| same run also removes the marked block from that exact file, so a block left
0105| behind by an install that edited a custom profile — including an install that
0106| wrote the block and then failed its fresh-shell check — does not survive. A file
0107| that is missing or carries no marker is left alone, no file is created, and the
0108| rest of each edited file is left unchanged.
0109| 
0110| Windows is not the main installation method; the fallback there is `python -m pip install --user` of the pinned revision.
0111| 
0112| ## Interactive session
0113| 
0114| Starting `forgel-code` with no arguments opens an interactive session instead of
0115| printing usage text. It shows a prompt and stays open until you leave, so you
0116| work by writing sentences rather than by translating every intent into a
0117| command.
0118| 
0119| Each sentence is handed to the engine's project agent as one free-form request
0120| and the agent's answer is shown in the session. The session also shows the
0121| project it is working on, and re-reads the task and release state from the
0122| engine on its own, so progress becomes visible without asking for a status
0123| again.
0124| 
0125| Some sentences ask the session for one specific action:
0126| 
0127| | You write | What the session asks the engine for |
0128| | --- | --- |
0129| | a plain sentence | the project agent's answer |
0130| | `plan <goal>` | a plan for the goal, shown with its tasks in plan order and their states |
0131| | `accept <task>` | accepting that task |
0132| | `rework <task> <remarks>` | sending that task back with the remarks |
0133| | `retry <task>` | retrying that task |
0134| | `pause` | pausing work |
0135| | `resume` | resuming work |
0136| | `switch to <key>` | selecting another project; every later request and every later state shown uses the new project |
0137| | `leave`, `exit`, `quit`, or the end of the input | ending the session |
0138| 
0139| A sentence that names no action, or more than one, gets a clarification and
0140| nothing is carried out. A request that becomes a plan shows its tasks in plan
0141| order, and one that becomes a task shows that task with its title and state.
0142| When an engine call fails, the session shows the reason and the next possible
0143| step and stays usable for the next request; leaving after a failure needs no
0144| restart. Replies follow the language of your message.
0145| 
0146| Adopting a repository, creating a project, setting or changing a secret and
0147| changing configuration are not part of the conversation. A sentence never
0148| carries them out; the session only points you to the explicit command for them.
0149| 
0150| Leaving ends the session at once: the client sends nothing further to the
0151| engine and keeps no transcript. Key material never reaches the screen, because
0152| a value that names a secret is replaced before it is shown.
0153| 
0154| The interactive session adds no capability of its own: every answer and every
0155| piece of state comes from the engine, and the client still calls no model, reads
0156| no project and runs no check. All commands below keep working one-shot, with the
0157| same output, exit status and `--json` form as before.
0158| 
0159| ## Commands
0160| 
0161| Every client command is a thin wrapper over an existing engine command, and
0162| the engine is always called with `--json`. `<key>` below is the project the
0163| client session selected with `forgel-code use`; while nothing is selected the
0164| client passes no `--project` and the engine keeps its own active project.
0165| 
0166| | Client command | Engine command | Purpose |
0167| | --- | --- | --- |
0168| | `forgel-code say <phrase>` | `forgel say "<phrase>"` | Turn a free phrase into a task |
0169| | `forgel-code status` | `forgel status` | State of the task and the milestone |
0170| | `forgel-code tasks` | `forgel tasks` | List tasks |
0171| | `forgel-code task <task>` | `forgel tasks` | State of one task, picked out of the engine's task list |
0172| | `forgel-code accept <task>` | `forgel task accept --task <task> [--project <key>]` | Accept a task |
0173| | `forgel-code rework <task> <remark...>` | `forgel task reject --task <task> --notes "<remark>" [--project <key>]` | Send a task back for rework with remarks |
0174| | `forgel-code resume` | `forgel resume` | Start or resume work |
0175| | `forgel-code pause` | `forgel pause` | Pause work |
0176| | `forgel-code plan "<goal>" [--milestone <key>]` | `forgel plan [<key>] --goal "<goal>"` | Decompose the milestone goal into tasks |
0177| | `forgel-code history` | `forgel history` | Short session history |
0178| | `forgel-code projects` | `forgel projects` | List projects |
0179| | `forgel-code session` | `forgel session` | Show the session the engine reports |
0180| | `forgel-code use <key>` | `forgel use <key>` | Select the active project |
0181| 
0182| `forgel-code` does not read a project itself: `task <task>` asks the engine for
0183| its task list and shows the one task you named. If that task is not in the
0184| engine's answer — or appears there more than once — the client reports it and
0185| exits with a non-zero code.
0186| 
0187| `accept` and `rework` lean on the engine's `task` command and its positional
0188| actions: accepting is `task accept`, sending back is `task reject`, and the
0189| remarks travel in the engine's `--notes`. The client adds no subcommand and no
0190| option of its own. The exact engine calls behind them are:
0191| 
0192| ```sh
0193| forgel task accept --task <task> --json
0194| forgel task reject --task <task> --notes "<remark>" --json
0195| ```
0196| 
0197| When the running engine does not provide the action a point needs, the client
0198| prints the engine's own message plus an explicit note ("no engine command for
0199| this point") and exits with a non-zero code instead of inventing behaviour.

1222| def _alpha_runs(text: str) -> List[str]:
1223|     """The runs of letters in ``text``, in order."""
1224|     runs: List[str] = []
1225|     current: List[str] = []
1226|     for character in text:
1227|         if character.isalpha():
1228|             current.append(character)
1229|         elif current:
1230|             runs.append("".join(current))
1231|             current = []
1232|     if current:
1233|         runs.append("".join(current))
1234|     return runs

1237| def _fold(text: str) -> str:
1238|     """The text lower-cased, without diacritics, its whitespace collapsed."""
1239|     decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", text)
1240|     plain = "".join(
1241|         character for character in decomposed if not unicodedata.combining(character)
1242|     )
1243|     return " ".join(plain.lower().split())

1246| def _asks_for_sensitive_action(folded: str) -> bool:
1247|     """Whether a folded sentence asks for a sensitive action in French or Spanish.
1248| 
1249|     The request needs the verb of the action and the object it acts on, in
1250|     either order; a sentence that names only one of them stays ordinary
1251|     conversation.
1252|     """
1253|     words = _alpha_runs(folded)
1254|     if not words:
1255|         return False
1256|     sequence = " " + " ".join(words) + " "
1257|     for (forms, stems), nouns in SENSITIVE_ACTIONS:
1258|         if not any(word in forms or word.startswith(stems) for word in words):
1259|             continue
1260|         if any((" " + noun + " ") in sequence for noun in nouns):
1261|             return True
1262|     return False

1265| def _elides(lowered: str) -> bool:
1266|     """Whether the text carries an elision characteristic of French."""
1267|     for index, character in enumerate(lowered):
1268|         if character not in APOSTROPHES:
1269|             continue
1270|         if index + 1 >= len(lowered) or not lowered[index + 1].isalpha():
1271|             continue
1272|         start = index
1273|         while start > 0 and lowered[start - 1].isalpha():
1274|             start -= 1
1275|         if lowered[start:index] in FRENCH_ELISIONS:
1276|             return True
1277|     return False

1280| def language_of(text: str, current: str = "en") -> str:
1281|     """The language of the owner's message, as far as a reply must follow it.
1282| 
1283|     Russian is the language of Cyrillic text, French and Spanish are recognised
1284|     by the letters, words and elisions only they use, and other Latin text is
1285|     English. A message that carries no language signal at all keeps the
1286|     language the session is already using.
1287|     """
1288|     if any("\u0400" <= character <= "\u04ff" for character in text):
1289|         return "ru"
1290|     lowered = text.lower()
1291|     french = sum(1 for character in lowered if character in FRENCH_LETTERS)
1292|     spanish = sum(1 for character in lowered if character in SPANISH_LETTERS)
1293|     for run in _alpha_runs(lowered):
1294|         if run in FRENCH_WORDS:
1295|             french += 1
1296|         elif run in SPANISH_WORDS:
1297|             spanish += 1
1298|     if _elides(lowered):
1299|         french += 1
1300|     if french > spanish:
1301|         return "fr"
1302|     if spanish > french:
1303|         return "es"
1304|     if any(len(run) > 1 for run in _alpha_runs(text)):
1305|         return "en"
1306|     return current

1413| def _span(text: str, start: int) -> Optional[Tuple[int, int]]:
1414|     """The characters of the one value at ``start``, a quoted run included.
1415| 
1416|     The span is exactly what the marker replaces, so the quotation marks that
1417|     dress a value stay visible around it.
1418|     """
1419|     if start >= len(text) or text[start].isspace():
1420|         return None
1421|     if text.startswith(REDACTED, start):
1422|         return start, start + len(REDACTED)
1423|     closing = _QUOTE_PAIRS.get(text[start])
1424|     if closing is not None:
1425|         limit = len(text)
1426|         newline = text.find("\n", start)
1427|         if newline >= 0:
1428|             limit = newline
1429|         found = text.find(closing, start + 1, limit)
1430|         if found < 0:
1431|             # An unclosed quote hides the rest of its line behind the quote.
1432|             return start + 1, limit
1433|         return start + 1, found
1434|     if text[start] in _NOT_A_VALUE:
1435|         return None
1436|     end = start
1437|     while end < len(text) and not text[end].isspace():
1438|         end += 1
1439|     while end > start + 1 and text[end - 1] in _TRAILING:
1440|         end -= 1
1441|     return start, end

1444| def _marked_span(text: str, start: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
1445|     """The punctuation at ``start`` and the value it introduces.
1446| 
1447|     A bracketed run is hidden whole, the brackets included; any other
1448|     punctuation belongs to the value that follows it, on the value's own line.
1449|     """
1450|     limit = len(text)
1451|     newline = text.find("\n", start)
1452|     if newline >= 0:
1453|         limit = newline
1454|     closing = _VALUE_BRACKETS.get(text[start])
1455|     if closing is not None:
1456|         found = text.find(closing, start + 1, limit)
1457|         if found >= 0:
1458|             return start, found + 1
1459|     end = start
1460|     while end < limit and not text[end].isspace():
1461|         end += 1
1462|     while end > start + 1 and text[end - 1] in _TRAILING:
1463|         end -= 1
1464|     return start, end

1467| def _explicit_span(text: str, start: int) -> Optional[Tuple[int, int]]:
1468|     """The value after an explicit ':' or '=' separator, if there is one.
1469| 
1470|     Quotation marks still stay visible around the marker; punctuation that
1471|     introduces the value becomes part of it, so the marker replaces both.
1472|     """
1473|     if start >= len(text) or text[start].isspace():
1474|         return None
1475|     if text.startswith(REDACTED, start):
1476|         return start, start + len(REDACTED)
1477|     if text[start] in _QUOTE_PAIRS:
1478|         return _span(text, start)
1479|     if text[start].isalnum() or text[start] == "_":
1480|         return _span(text, start)
1481|     span = _marked_span(text, start)
1482|     if not any(character.isalnum() for character in text[span[0]:span[1]]):
1483|         # Punctuation alone carries no value: the label is merely punctuated.
1484|         return None
1485|     return span

1492|     run is masked.

1494|     position = start
1495|     while position < len(text) and (
1496|         text[position] in "=:" or text[position] in _WHITESPACE
1497|     ):

0001| # code
0002| 
0003| Forgel Code — thin console client for Forgel over the engine's machine-readable
0004| commands.
0005| 
0006| The client does not import the engine. Its only channel is running
0007| `forgel <command> --json` as a separate process and reading exactly one JSON
0008| object from stdout. The model, sandbox, independent QA, review and release
0009| approval stay in the engine: the client never calls a model, never reads
0010| project files and never runs checks itself.
0011| 
0012| ## Install
0013| 
0014| Forgel Code installs with one command. It needs Python 3.9 or newer with the
0015| `pip` module it ships, and the `forgel` engine on `PATH`.
0016| 
0017| ```sh
0018| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.1/install.sh | sh
0019| ```
0020| 
0021| The installer puts the client into `~/.local/share/forgel-code` and a
0022| `forgel-code` launcher into `~/.local/bin`, then adds that directory to `PATH`
0023| through one marked block in the profile your login shell reads. No virtual
0024| environment and no activation step are involved, and the same command run again
0025| replaces the installation instead of duplicating anything.
0026| 
0027| | Login shell | Profile file that receives the block |
0028| | --- | --- |
0029| | zsh | `~/.zshrc` |
0030| | bash | the first existing of `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`, `~/.profile`; `~/.bash_profile` is created when none of them exists |
0031| | other POSIX `sh` | `~/.profile`, with a warning on stderr that names the file and the detected shell |
0032| 
0033| The login shell comes from `$SHELL`. When that is unset, empty or names a shell
0034| the installer does not handle, it reads the shell of the invoking process and
0035| then the account login shell — the macOS Directory Service entry, otherwise the
0036| passwd entry — and only then falls back to `~/.profile`. The block is never
0037| written to `~/.bashrc` alone, because a login bash shell does not read that
0038| file. A profile file that does not exist yet is created.
0039| 
0040| The block carries a `case "$PATH:"` guard and prepends the launcher directory
0041| only when it is not already there, so sourcing it again, or sourcing several
0042| profiles that carry it, leaves exactly one entry. There is no unguarded
0043| `export PATH=...` line.
0044| 
0045| After writing the block the installer checks it: it starts the detected login
0046| shell as a login interactive shell from a cleared environment, under a bounded
0047| time limit enforced without GNU `timeout`, and requires `command -v forgel-code`
0048| to resolve to the launcher it just wrote. On success it prints the detected
0049| shell, the edited profile file and the path that fresh shell resolved. If the
0050| check fails, or the shell does not answer within the limit, it exits non-zero
0051| and prints on stderr the edited profile file, the exact block it wrote, the
0052| shell it checked, the `PATH` that shell saw and what `forgel-code` resolved to,
0053| so a profile your login shell never reads is never reported as active.
0054| Re-running keeps exactly one marked block and leaves the rest of the file as it
0055| was.
0056| 
0057| The client has no dependencies and builds through the small in-tree PEP 517
0058| backend (`_build_backend.py`), so the installer never needs a package index.
0059| Editable installs are not supported: the backend implements only the
0060| `build_wheel` and `build_sdist` hooks.
0061| 
0062| ### Options
0063| 
0064| | Variable | Effect |
0065| | --- | --- |
0066| | `FORGEL_CODE_HOME` | installation prefix (default `~/.local/share/forgel-code`) |
0067| | `FORGEL_CODE_BIN` | directory of the `forgel-code` launcher (default `~/.local/bin`) |
0068| | `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` | shell profile that receives the `PATH` block, instead of the detected one; the uninstall cleans it too |
0069| | `FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH` | set it to leave the shell profile untouched |
0070| | `FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE` | install from a local checkout instead of the network |
0071| 
0072| With `FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1` no profile file is opened for writing, no
0073| fresh-shell check runs, the installer prints the exact line to add yourself and
0074| exits with code 0.
0075| 
0076| ```sh
0077| export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
0078| ```
0079| 
0080| ```sh
0081| FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE=/path/to/code sh install.sh
0082| ```
0083| 
0084| The `forgel` engine must be available on `PATH`; use `--engine PATH` or
0085| `$FORGEL_ENGINE` to point at a specific binary. `forgel-code --version` prints
0086| the installed version.
0087| 
0088| ### Update
0089| 
0090| ```sh
0091| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.1/install.sh | sh
0092| ```
0093| 
0094| ### Uninstall
0095| 
0096| ```sh
0097| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.1/install.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall
0098| ```
0099| 
0100| The uninstall removes the installation prefix, the `forgel-code` launcher and
0101| the marked `PATH` block from every profile file this installer can have written:
0102| `~/.zshrc`, `~/.zprofile`, `~/.zshenv`, `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`,
0103| `~/.profile` and `~/.bashrc`. When `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` names another file, the
0104| same run also removes the marked block from that exact file, so a block left
0105| behind by an install that edited a custom profile — including an install that
0106| wrote the block and then failed its fresh-shell check — does not survive. A file
0107| that is missing or carries no marker is left alone, no file is created, and the
0108| rest of each edited file is left unchanged.
0109| 
0110| Windows is not the main installation method; the fallback there is `python -m pip install --user` of the pinned revision.
0111| 
0112| ## Interactive session
0113| 
0114| Starting `forgel-code` with no arguments opens an interactive session instead of
0115| printing usage text. It shows a prompt and stays open until you leave, so you
0116| work by writing sentences rather than by translating every intent into a
0117| command.
0118| 
0119| Each sentence is handed to the engine's project agent as one free-form request
0120| and the agent's answer is shown in the session. The session also shows the
0121| project it is working on, and re-reads the task and release state from the
0122| engine on its own, so progress becomes visible without asking for a status
0123| again.
0124| 
0125| Some sentences ask the session for one specific action:
0126| 
0127| | You write | What the session asks the engine for |
0128| | --- | --- |
0129| | a plain sentence | the project agent's answer |
0130| | `plan <goal>` | a plan for the goal, shown with its tasks in plan order and their states |
0131| | `accept <task>` | accepting that task |
0132| | `rework <task> <remarks>` | sending that task back with the remarks |
0133| | `retry <task>` | retrying that task |
0134| | `pause` | pausing work |
0135| | `resume` | resuming work |
0136| | `switch to <key>` | selecting another project; every later request and every later state shown uses the new project |
0137| | `leave`, `exit`, `quit`, or the end of the input | ending the session |
0138| 
0139| A sentence that names no action, or more than one, gets a clarification and
0140| nothing is carried out. A request that becomes a plan shows its tasks in plan
0141| order, and one that becomes a task shows that task with its title and state.
0142| When an engine call fails, the session shows the reason and the next possible
0143| step and stays usable for the next request; leaving after a failure needs no
0144| restart. Replies follow the language of your message.
0145| 
0146| Adopting a repository, creating a project, setting or changing a secret and
0147| changing configuration are not part of the conversation. A sentence never
0148| carries them out; the session only points you to the explicit command for them.
0149| 
0150| Leaving ends the session at once: the client sends nothing further to the
0151| engine and keeps no transcript. Key material never reaches the screen, because
0152| a value that names a secret is replaced before it is shown.
0153| 
0154| The interactive session adds no capability of its own: every answer and every
0155| piece of state comes from the engine, and the client still calls no model, reads
0156| no project and runs no check. All commands below keep working one-shot, with the
0157| same output, exit status and `--json` form as before.
0158| 
0159| ## Commands
0160| 
0161| Every client command is a thin wrapper over an existing engine command, and
0162| the engine is always called with `--json`. `<key>` below is the project the
0163| client session selected with `forgel-code use`; while nothing is selected the
0164| client passes no `--project` and the engine keeps its own active project.
0165| 
0166| | Client command | Engine command | Purpose |
0167| | --- | --- | --- |
0168| | `forgel-code say <phrase>` | `forgel say "<phrase>"` | Turn a free phrase into a task |
0169| | `forgel-code status` | `forgel status` | State of the task and the milestone |
0170| | `forgel-code tasks` | `forgel tasks` | List tasks |
0171| | `forgel-code task <task>` | `forgel tasks` | State of one task, picked out of the engine's task list |
0172| | `forgel-code accept <task>` | `forgel task accept --task <task> [--project <key>]` | Accept a task |
0173| | `forgel-code rework <task> <remark...>` | `forgel task reject --task <task> --notes "<remark>" [--project <key>]` | Send a task back for rework with remarks |
0174| | `forgel-code resume` | `forgel resume` | Start or resume work |
0175| | `forgel-code pause` | `forgel pause` | Pause work |
0176| | `forgel-code plan "<goal>" [--milestone <key>]` | `forgel plan [<key>] --goal "<goal>"` | Decompose the milestone goal into tasks |
0177| | `forgel-code history` | `forgel history` | Short session history |
0178| | `forgel-code projects` | `forgel projects` | List projects |
0179| | `forgel-code session` | `forgel session` | Show the session the engine reports |
0180| | `forgel-code use <key>` | `forgel use <key>` | Select the active project |
0181| 
0182| `forgel-code` does not read a project itself: `task <task>` asks the engine for
0183| its task list and shows the one task you named. If that task is not in the
0184| engine's answer — or appears there more than once — the client reports it and
0185| exits with a non-zero code.
0186| 
0187| `accept` and `rework` lean on the engine's `task` command and its positional
0188| actions: accepting is `task accept`, sending back is `task reject`, and the
0189| remarks travel in the engine's `--notes`. The client adds no subcommand and no
0190| option of its own. The exact engine calls behind them are:
0191| 
0192| ```sh
0193| forgel task accept --task <task> --json
0194| forgel task reject --task <task> --notes "<remark>" --json
0195| ```
0196| 
0197| When the running engine does not provide the action a point needs, the client
0198| prints the engine's own message plus an explicit note ("no engine command for
0199| this point") and exits with a non-zero code instead of inventing behaviour.
0200| That decision is taken from the engine's return code and structured error
0201| fields, never from the wording of its message, so it does not depend on the
0202| locale.
0203| 
0204| ### Output
0205| 
0206| Without a flag a command prints human readable text. With `--json` it prints
0207| exactly one JSON object to stdout:
0208| 
0209| ```json
0210| {"command": "status", "project": "acme", "ok": true, "result": {}}
0211| ```
0212| 
0213| The `project` field is the project key actually handed to the engine, or `null`
0214| when nothing was passed. On failure — including an argument-parse error — the
0215| client exits with a non-zero code and, with `--json`, prints one JSON object
0216| with `"ok": false` and the message under `error`. A structured engine refusal
0217| (`"ok": false` in the engine's answer) is a failure even when the engine exits
0218| with code 0, and its own fields are carried through. A failure report names the
0219| engine that answered: the path configured by `--engine`, `$FORGEL_ENGINE` or
0220| `forgel` leads the message.
0221| 
0222| ### Active project
0223| 
0224| `forgel-code use <key>` hands the key to the engine and, only when the engine
0225| accepts it, makes it the active project; every project-scoped command then
0226| passes `--project <key>`. `forgel-code projects` lists what the engine knows
0227| about. Until you pick a key no `--project` argument is sent, so the engine's own
0228| active project is used. Set `FORGEL_CODE_HOME` to move the session file.
0229| 
0230| ### Timeout
0231| 
0232| The engine call is bounded. `--timeout SECONDS` sets the limit for one call,
0233| `$FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT` sets it for the environment, and the default is 600
0234| seconds. When the limit elapses the client kills the engine and fails with a
0235| structured error instead of blocking. The engine's stdout is always decoded as
0236| UTF-8 and the child process does not receive the client's stdin.
0237| 
0238| `--json`, `--engine` and `--timeout` are parsed as options of their own and are
0239| never substituted inside argument text, so a phrase or remark that mentions
0240| such a word reaches the engine unchanged. Put `--` before a remark that itself
0241| begins with a hyphen.

0001| # Changelog
0002| 
0003| All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.
0004| 
0005| The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
0006| and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
0007| 
0008| ## [Unreleased]
0009| 
0010| ### Added
0011| 
0012| - Open an interactive session when the client starts with no arguments — `forgel-code` now shows a prompt and stays open instead of printing usage text. A sentence typed at the prompt is handed to the engine's project agent as one free-form request and the agent's answer is shown in the session. The session shows the selected project and lets the owner switch it without leaving, shows a plan as its ordered tasks with their states and a new task with its title and state, and re-reads the task and release state from the engine on its own so progress appears without asking for a status. Accepting a task, sending it back with remarks, retrying a failed task, pausing and resuming work are asked for in plain language, an ambiguous or unmatched request gets a clarification and performs nothing, a failure shows the reason and the next possible step while the session stays usable, and replies follow the language of the owner's message. Adopting a repository, creating a project, secrets and configuration stay explicit separate actions that a sentence never triggers, key material never reaches the screen, and leaving — or the end of the input — ends the session at once. The session adds no capability: every answer and every piece of state still comes from the engine, and every one-shot usage keeps its previous output, exit status and `--json` form.
0013| 
0014| ### Changed
0015| 
0016| - Speed up the suite without weakening a test — the expensive duplicated work is gone instead of a scenario: one read-only checkout copy and one prepared installation per scenario group are shared by the tests that only read them, and the bounded-check cases configure a limit below the product default.
0017| - Remove every statement of a suite completion time, duration or runtime bound from the documentation — the README `## Tests` section still says that one documented command runs the whole suite, that the installer situations are covered by a real installation into a throwaway home location with a real detected login shell, and that a run from a source checkout needs only the Python standard library and no network access, but it no longer promises how long such a run takes.
0018| 
0019| ### Fixed
0020| 
0021| - Mask the credential of a label followed by an ordinary descriptor word — a secret label followed by a word such as `value`, `field` or `string` used to hide that descriptor and leave the credential itself on screen and in the retained state; the descriptor now stays readable and the value, including the one behind a copula or a separator, is replaced by the existing masking placeholder. Sentences that only mention a secret word are still shown unchanged.
0022| - Remove the PATH block from the profile named by `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` — `--uninstall` again cleans the marked block out of the profile the override variable names, in addition to the six standard profile files, so a block left by a completed install or by an install that failed its fresh-shell check no longer survives.
0023| - Point the README install, update and uninstall commands at the current `v0.1.1` release installer — the documented commands no longer fetch the stale install script, all three name one and the same install-script URL, and the guard in `tests/test_readme_install.py` fails the suite when any of them carries an older tag or a divergent install-script URL.
0024| 
0025| ## [0.1.1] - 2026-11-23
0026| 
0027| ### Fixed
0028| 
0029| - Fix install.sh so a new terminal finds forgel-code on PATH — The installer currently completes while the launcher directory never reaches PATH in a freshly opened terminal. It picks the profile file from $SHELL alone: on macOS a bash login shell never reads ~/.bashrc, and under `curl … | sh` $SHELL can be empty, sending the block to ~/.profile while the terminal reads ~/.zshrc. It also never checks that its own change took effect. This change makes the installer detect the real login shell, write the block into a profile file a new terminal actually reads, start a clean login shell afterwards and verify that `forgel-code` resolves, and fail with a message naming the edited file and the observed PATH when it does not. --uninstall removes the block from every profile file the installer can have written.
0030| - Release audit: --uninstall no longer honors FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE. The old code removed the block — Add ${FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE:-} to the uninstall candidate set when it is set (deduplicate against PROFILE_NAMES), and add a test that installs and uninstalls with a custom profile path.
0031| - Release audit: --uninstall omits ~/.bashrc, although the previous installer wrote the marked bl — Include ~/.bashrc in the legacy cleanup set for uninstall, update the README list, and extend CANDIDATE_PROFILES/test_uninstall_clears_every_candidate_profile to cover it.

0001| # code
0002| 
0003| Forgel Code — thin console client for Forgel over the engine's machine-readable
0004| commands.
0005| 
0006| The client does not import the engine. Its only channel is running
0007| `forgel <command> --json` as a separate process and reading exactly one JSON
0008| object from stdout. The model, sandbox, independent QA, review and release
0009| approval stay in the engine: the client never calls a model, never reads
0010| project files and never runs checks itself.
0011| 
0012| ## Install
0013| 
0014| Forgel Code installs with one command. It needs Python 3.9 or newer with the
0015| `pip` module it ships, and the `forgel` engine on `PATH`.
0016| 
0017| ```sh
0018| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.1/install.sh | sh
0019| ```
0020| 
0021| The installer puts the client into `~/.local/share/forgel-code` and a
0022| `forgel-code` launcher into `~/.local/bin`, then adds that directory to `PATH`
0023| through one marked block in the profile your login shell reads. No virtual
0024| environment and no activation step are involved, and the same command run again
0025| replaces the installation instead of duplicating anything.
0026| 
0027| | Login shell | Profile file that receives the block |
0028| | --- | --- |
0029| | zsh | `~/.zshrc` |
0030| | bash | the first existing of `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`, `~/.profile`; `~/.bash_profile` is created when none of them exists |
0031| | other POSIX `sh` | `~/.profile`, with a warning on stderr that names the file and the detected shell |
0032| 
0033| The login shell comes from `$SHELL`. When that is unset, empty or names a shell
0034| the installer does not handle, it reads the shell of the invoking process and
0035| then the account login shell — the macOS Directory Service entry, otherwise the
0036| passwd entry — and only then falls back to `~/.profile`. The block is never
0037| written to `~/.bashrc` alone, because a login bash shell does not read that
0038| file. A profile file that does not exist yet is created.
0039| 
0040| The block carries a `case "$PATH:"` guard and prepends the launcher directory
0041| only when it is not already there, so sourcing it again, or sourcing several
0042| profiles that carry it, leaves exactly one entry. There is no unguarded
0043| `export PATH=...` line.
0044| 
0045| After writing the block the installer checks it: it starts the detected login
0046| shell as a login interactive shell from a cleared environment, under a bounded
0047| time limit enforced without GNU `timeout`, and requires `command -v forgel-code`
0048| to resolve to the launcher it just wrote. On success it prints the detected
0049| shell, the edited profile file and the path that fresh shell resolved. If the
0050| check fails, or the shell does not answer within the limit, it exits non-zero
0051| and prints on stderr the edited profile file, the exact block it wrote, the
0052| shell it checked, the `PATH` that shell saw and what `forgel-code` resolved to,
0053| so a profile your login shell never reads is never reported as active.
0054| Re-running keeps exactly one marked block and leaves the rest of the file as it
0055| was.
0056| 
0057| The client has no dependencies and builds through the small in-tree PEP 517
0058| backend (`_build_backend.py`), so the installer never needs a package index.
0059| Editable installs are not supported: the backend implements only the
0060| `build_wheel` and `build_sdist` hooks.
0061| 
0062| ### Options
0063| 
0064| | Variable | Effect |
0065| | --- | --- |
0066| | `FORGEL_CODE_HOME` | installation prefix (default `~/.local/share/forgel-code`) |
0067| | `FORGEL_CODE_BIN` | directory of the `forgel-code` launcher (default `~/.local/bin`) |
0068| | `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` | shell profile that receives the `PATH` block, instead of the detected one; the uninstall cleans it too |
0069| | `FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH` | set it to leave the shell profile untouched |
0070| | `FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE` | install from a local checkout instead of the network |
0071| 
0072| With `FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1` no profile file is opened for writing, no
0073| fresh-shell check runs, the installer prints the exact line to add yourself and
0074| exits with code 0.
0075| 
0076| ```sh
0077| export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
0078| ```
0079| 
0080| ```sh
0081| FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE=/path/to/code sh install.sh
0082| ```
0083| 
0084| The `forgel` engine must be available on `PATH`; use `--engine PATH` or
0085| `$FORGEL_ENGINE` to point at a specific binary. `forgel-code --version` prints
0086| the installed version.
0087| 
0088| ### Update
0089| 
0090| ```sh
0091| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.1/install.sh | sh
0092| ```
0093| 
0094| ### Uninstall
0095| 
0096| ```sh
0097| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.1/install.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall
0098| ```
0099| 
0100| The uninstall removes the installation prefix, the `forgel-code` launcher and
0101| the marked `PATH` block from every profile file this installer can have written:
0102| `~/.zshrc`, `~/.zprofile`, `~/.zshenv`, `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`,
0103| `~/.profile` and `~/.bashrc`. When `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` names another file, the
0104| same run also removes the marked block from that exact file, so a block left
0105| behind by an install that edited a custom profile — including an install that
0106| wrote the block and then failed its fresh-shell check — does not survive. A file
0107| that is missing or carries no marker is left alone, no file is created, and the
0108| rest of each edited file is left unchanged.
0109| 
0110| Windows is not the main installation method; the fallback there is `python -m pip install --user` of the pinned revision.

0116| work by writing sentences rather than by translating every intent into a
0117| command.
0118| 
0119| Each sentence is handed to the engine's project agent as one free-form request
0120| and the agent's answer is shown in the session. The session also shows the

0128| | --- | --- |
0129| | a plain sentence | the project agent's answer |
0130| | `plan <goal>` | a plan for the goal, shown with its tasks in plan order and their states |

0136| | `switch to <key>` | selecting another project; every later request and every later state shown uses the new project |
0137| | `leave`, `exit`, `quit`, or the end of the input | ending the session |
0138| 
0139| A sentence that names no action, or more than one, gets a clarification and
0140| nothing is carried out. A request that becomes a plan shows its tasks in plan
0141| order, and one that becomes a task shows that task with its title and state.
0142| When an engine call fails, the session shows the reason and the next possible
0143| step and stays usable for the next request; leaving after a failure needs no
0144| restart. Replies follow the language of your message.

0148| carries them out; the session only points you to the explicit command for them.

0151| engine and keeps no transcript. Key material never reaches the screen, because
0152| a value that names a secret is replaced before it is shown.
0153| 
0154| The interactive session adds no capability of its own: every answer and every
0155| piece of state comes from the engine, and the client still calls no model, reads
0156| no project and runs no check. All commands below keep working one-shot, with the
0157| same output, exit status and `--json` form as before.

0159| ## Commands
0160| 
0161| Every client command is a thin wrapper over an existing engine command, and
0162| the engine is always called with `--json`. `<key>` below is the project the
0163| client session selected with `forgel-code use`; while nothing is selected the
0164| client passes no `--project` and the engine keeps its own active project.
0165| 
0166| | Client command | Engine command | Purpose |
0167| | --- | --- | --- |
0168| | `forgel-code say <phrase>` | `forgel say "<phrase>"` | Turn a free phrase into a task |
0169| | `forgel-code status` | `forgel status` | State of the task and the milestone |
0170| | `forgel-code tasks` | `forgel tasks` | List tasks |
0171| | `forgel-code task <task>` | `forgel tasks` | State of one task, picked out of the engine's task list |
0172| | `forgel-code accept <task>` | `forgel task accept --task <task> [--project <key>]` | Accept a task |
0173| | `forgel-code rework <task> <remark...>` | `forgel task reject --task <task> --notes "<remark>" [--project <key>]` | Send a task back for rework with remarks |
0174| | `forgel-code resume` | `forgel resume` | Start or resume work |
0175| | `forgel-code pause` | `forgel pause` | Pause work |
0176| | `forgel-code plan "<goal>" [--milestone <key>]` | `forgel plan [<key>] --goal "<goal>"` | Decompose the milestone goal into tasks |
0177| | `forgel-code history` | `forgel history` | Short session history |
0178| | `forgel-code projects` | `forgel projects` | List projects |
0179| | `forgel-code session` | `forgel session` | Show the session the engine reports |
0180| | `forgel-code use <key>` | `forgel use <key>` | Select the active project |

0182| `forgel-code` does not read a project itself: `task <task>` asks the engine for
0183| its task list and shows the one task you named. If that task is not in the
